letter:
Dear Hiring Team,

I am applying for the Junior Software Engineer role with Example Hiring Team. I build accessible web applications and tested backend services, with a particular interest in reliable APIs and clear user workflows. Your need for Node.js API testing directly matches my experience, while my React and accessibility work provide a relevant foundation for the interface responsibilities. I am especially drawn to an early-career role that combines product-facing interface work with backend reliability.

At Example Studio, I built appointment-conflict validation in a Node.js API and added regression tests for overlapping bookings. I also replaced an inaccessible date picker with a keyboard-operated booking flow after testing it with the product team. This work connected backend correctness with a more accessible user workflow and strengthened my focus on testing behavior that directly affects users.

My independent Booking Lab project extends that focus. I built an appointment scheduler with persistent storage and automated tests for booking conflicts using TypeScript, React, Node.js, and PostgreSQL. I documented the tradeoff between database constraints and application validation and added a reproducible local demo. The project reflects how I work: make behavior testable, explain technical tradeoffs clearly, and keep development workflows reproducible.

I would bring hands-on experience in the role’s core API-testing area, plus practical work across accessible workflows and React-based application development. While Kubernetes operations are not yet part of my documented experience, I would approach them as a clear learning priority. I would welcome the opportunity to contribute my TypeScript, React, Node.js, PostgreSQL, Python, and Git skills while growing into the operational responsibilities of the role.

Kind regards,
Zoë Șerban
